hints: The normal passes through centre $(3, 1)$ and point $A(6, 5)$.
Write in $y = mx + c$ form: $y - 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x - 3) \implies y = \dfrac{4}{3}x - 3$.
walkthrough:
The normal follows the radius; the tangent is perpendicular to it.
Calculate the gradient of the normal passing through centre $(3, 1)$ and point $A(6, 5)$:
$$m_{\text{norm}} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{6 - 3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

Write the normal equation in slope-intercept form:
$$y - 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x - 3) \implies y = \dfrac{4}{3}x - 3$$

hints: The tangent gradient is perpendicular to the normal gradient: $m_\perp = -\dfrac{3}{4}$.
walkthrough:
The normal follows the radius; the tangent is perpendicular to it.
The tangent is perpendicular to the normal:
$$m_{\text{tan}} = -\dfrac{1}{4/3} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Write the tangent equation at $A(6, 5)$ in slope-intercept form:
$$y - 5 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 6)$$
$$y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + \dfrac{18}{4} + 5 = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + \dfrac{19}{2}$$
